findings.title: Expired spending leases can restart without the required checkpoint
findings.detail: S090 requires rejecting RESUME without a checkpoint. The takeover guard rejects a missing checkpoint only when OLD.checkpoint_hash is non-null, so an expired JOB_ATTEMPT or MODEL_TASK that never checkpointed can be claimed by another owner with null and receive a new fence. Additionally, claim_lease's same-owner branch at line 243 executes before the expiry check and ignores p_checkpoint entirely: an expired owner can restart with a missing or incorrect checkpoint while retaining its old fence. The two cited S090 tests exercise only different-owner takeovers after storing a checkpoint, leaving both paths untested.
findings.reproduction: Using PgLeaseStore under kauro_control, claim a new JOB_ATTEMPT at t0 with ttlSeconds=120, deadlineAt=t0+3600s, a valid subject hash, a costAuthorityId and checkpointHash=null. Commit without checkpointing. Claim the same resource at t0+130s with another owner and identical immutable fields, again checkpointHash=null: the SQL returns CLAIMED with fence 2 instead of refusing. Separately, store a checkpoint during the first live lease, then claim after expiry using the original owner and checkpointHash=null or a different hash: it returns CLAIMED with fence 1. These follow directly from lines 200-208 and 243-259; the read-only review did not rerun PostgreSQL.

findings.title: ApprovePlan accepts sources whose retention has already expired
findings.detail: CMD025-DENY requires an expired source to require new review. The handler checks only source.state === SEALED. PgDatasetRevisionRepository.lockSealedByHash (workspace.ts:309) reads no retention deadline, so approval remains possible after the governing retention deadline passes and before the sweeper changes the revision state. The existing product availability reader explicitly requires an ACTIVE retention record with effective_deadline > kauro.server_now() (packages/persistence/src/source/readers.ts:34). The passing CMD025 success test already exercises this defect: cmd025-approve-plan.test.ts:73 calls approvable without recent=true; support.ts:682 uses the default source fixture, whose seal is approximately fifteen days old and whose UNPAID retention expires fourteen days after sealing (source-lifecycle.ts:154,613). It nevertheless commits a live approval.
findings.reproduction: Follow the existing test titled 'OK: an APPROVER with a fresh step-up approves a VALIDATED plan whose receipt, source and target are current; the approval hash binds the named preimage'. Keep its default approvable fixture, authorized approver, fresh proof and test-bound disclosure composer. Read the source's retention record: effective_deadline is already past, while dataset_revisions.state remains SEALED. POST the matching approval body. The recorded test returns 201 and asserts a live approval and APPROVED plan; the registry requires SOURCE_EXPIRED and no approval. Alternatively, let a current source's retention expire without running the sweeper and submit the same otherwise valid request.

findings.title: Three RACE rows narrow the registry outcome and overclaim complete execution
findings.detail: CMD023-RACE, CMD025-RACE (line 107) and CMD026-RACE (line 110) replace their registry expected outcomes with retry/conflict/crash descriptions and claim EXECUTED_LOCAL for the whole case. briefs.md retains each command's full successful effect plus concurrency requirements. The same map correctly marks CMD023-OK PARTIAL because patch resolution/compilation is test-bound and owned by B03/B08, CMD025-OK PARTIAL because exact disclosure composition is simulated and owned by B08, and CMD026-OK PARTIAL because active-work cancellation/reconciliation is not demonstrated and belongs to B08. Their race tests prove the real PostgreSQL transaction protocol, but do not remove these dependencies or demonstrate those omitted clauses.
findings.reproduction: Compare the three RACE expectations in briefs.md with case-map lines 104, 107 and 110, then read their exact cited tests: cmd023-revise-plan.test.ts :: 'RACE: two revisions on one version → one successor; identical retry replays; the same key with another patch → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; crash leaves the predecessor unsuperseded and the same key then revises it once'; cmd025-approve-plan.test.ts :: 'RACE: two approvers on one version → one 201, one 409; identical retry replays; conflicting → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; a crash before COMMIT leaves the plan VALIDATED with no approval and the same key then approves it once'; cmd026-withdraw-approval.test.ts :: 'RACE: two withdrawals → one 200, one 409; identical retry replays; a withdrawal cannot be undone (KA004)'. The first two run with world()'s test plan services; the third asserts withdrawal rows/events without executing the B08 cancellation/reconciliation consumer. Retain EXECUTED_LOCAL for the demonstrated protocol clauses, mark the complete cases PARTIAL, and name the simulated/deferred clauses.
